description: MariaDB 11.4 LTS health metric catalog. Derived from dbi services scoring framework. Technology-specific implementation of the universal pillar/subcategory structure. Metric semantics validated against MariaDB 11.4 LTS and 11.7 / 11.8 rolling releases. MariaDB-specific features: Galera Cluster, built-in thread pool, Aria engine, system versioning, ed25519 auth, file_key_management TDE.
release_notes: v1.3.1 (2026-09-23): catalog maturity label added (draft: not yet reviewed by a technology leader, neither for collection nor for scoring). No metric, threshold, weight or rule change. v1.3.0 (PoC): seven hot metrics refactored to use scoring-core v1.5.0 profile-keyed thresholds, plus two long-flagged placement moves applied. Affected metrics: CAP-3.2 (purge_lag profile-keyed), PERF-3.1 (innodb_row_lock_waits profile-keyed), PERF-1.1 (buffer_pool_hit_ratio profile-keyed), CAP-3.1 (innodb_buffer_pool_hit_rate MOVED to perf_cache + profile-keyed), CAP-2.5 (thread_cache_hit_rate MOVED to perf_cache), PERF-2.6 (full_table_scan_rate profile-keyed), PERF-3.3 (metadata_lock_waits profile-keyed). v1.2.0: schema-ready for consistency_rules (rules deferred to Technology Leader work). v1.1.0: Subcategory point allocations within Capacity, Performance, and Future-Proofing pillars differ from the architecture specification (SCORING_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md section 2.3). These splits have been stable since v1.0.0 and are flagged for tech-leader review. See docs/guides/metric-placement-review.md for details.

metrics.description: Whether the MariaDB binary log (log_bin) is on. Required for point-in-time recovery and replication.
metrics.remediation: Enable binary logging: log_bin = /var/lib/mysql/mysql-bin in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether the binary log format (binlog_format) is ROW. Required for reliable replication and PITR.
metrics.remediation: Set binlog_format = ROW in my.cnf for reliable replication and PITR

metrics.description: Binary log retention window (binlog_expire_logs_seconds). Should fall in the 1-30 day range to support PITR without exhausting disk.
metrics.remediation: Set expire_logs_days = 7 (or binlog_expire_logs_seconds) in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether MariaDB GTID mode is on (gtid_slave_pos or gtid_current_pos). Required for reliable replication and PITR.
metrics.remediation: Enable GTID: set gtid_strict_mode = ON and use gtid_current_pos or gtid_slave_pos

metrics.description: Whether the binary log is flushed per transaction (sync_binlog=1). Required to avoid losing committed transactions on crash.
metrics.remediation: Set sync_binlog = 1 in my.cnf for crash-safe binary logging

metrics.description: Whether a regular backup cadence (daily, hourly, continuous, or binlog-only) is in place. Required to keep RPO bounded.
metrics.remediation: Document and implement a backup schedule (daily recommended)

metrics.description: Age of the most recent successful backup. Stale backups widen the worst-case data-loss window.
metrics.remediation: Verify backup jobs are running and completing successfully

metrics.description: Whether a logical backup (mariadb-dump or mariadb-backup) runs on a schedule. Complements physical backups for portability and partial restores.
metrics.remediation: Schedule regular mariadb-dump for logical backup in addition to physical backups

metrics.description: Whether backups are periodically verified for integrity. Untested backups risk silent corruption discovered only at recovery time.
metrics.remediation: Implement backup verification process (restore tests on non-production)

metrics.description: Whether mariadb-backup (or compatible XtraBackup fork) is used for hot physical backups. Required for online consistent backups of InnoDB.
metrics.remediation: Install mariadb-backup for consistent online physical backups (replaces XtraBackup for MariaDB)

metrics.description: Whether point-in-time recovery via binary logs is available. Without it, recovery is limited to the most recent full backup.
metrics.remediation: Enable binary logging and test PITR procedures using mariadb-binlog

metrics.description: Whether backup files are encrypted at rest. Required to protect data leaks via stolen or misplaced backup media.
metrics.remediation: Enable backup encryption using mariadb-backup --encrypt or encrypted storage

metrics.description: Whether a replica (ideally a delayed one) exists as a DR target. Provides a fast failover and protection against logical corruption.
metrics.remediation: Configure a delayed replica (CHANGE MASTER TO ... MASTER_DELAY = N) for DR

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) target is documented. Without an RPO target, backup cadence cannot be evaluated against business need.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RPO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) target is documented. Without an RTO target, recovery tooling and HA design cannot be sized.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RTO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether a restore drill has been performed within the last 90 days. Untested restore procedures are a top cause of failed recoveries.
metrics.remediation: Schedule regular restore tests (at least quarterly)

metrics.description: Whether a disaster recovery plan and runbook exist. Required to coordinate response under time pressure during an incident.
metrics.remediation: Document disaster recovery procedures and runbooks

metrics.description: Whether backup retention duration matches organizational and regulatory policy. Short retention can defeat compliance and forensic recovery.
metrics.remediation: Configure backup retention to meet compliance requirements

metrics.description: Whether binary log retention covers the required PITR window. If logs expire too early, recovery to a recent point becomes impossible.
metrics.remediation: Ensure expire_logs_days covers required recovery window

metrics.description: Whether backups exist on offsite or independent storage. Local-only backups are lost together with the primary in a site disaster.
metrics.remediation: Implement offsite backup copies to S3, Azure Blob, or remote storage

metrics.description: Share of client connections using TLS encryption. Cleartext connections expose credentials and payloads on the network.
metrics.remediation: Set require_secure_transport = ON in my.cnf and configure clients to use TLS

metrics.description: Whether accounts use a modern auth plugin (ed25519 or caching_sha2_password). Legacy plugins weaken password storage and TLS handshake.
metrics.remediation: Migrate accounts to ed25519 plugin: ALTER USER x IDENTIFIED VIA ed25519 USING PASSWORD('...')

metrics.description: Whether a password-strength plugin (simple_password_check or cracklib_password_check) is loaded. Required to enforce minimum password complexity.
metrics.remediation: INSTALL PLUGIN simple_password_check SONAME 'simple_password_check.so'

metrics.description: Volume of failed login attempts in the last 24h. Spikes can indicate brute-force or credential-stuffing activity.
metrics.remediation: Investigate failed login sources; enable connection_control plugin

metrics.description: Whether a server-wide password expiry policy (default_password_lifetime) is set. Indefinite passwords compound credential-leak risk over time.
metrics.remediation: Set default_password_lifetime = 90 in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether the server enforces TLS for every client (require_secure_transport). Without it, plaintext connections remain possible.
metrics.remediation: Set require_secure_transport = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Minimum negotiated TLS version (tls_version). TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated and vulnerable; 1.2+ is required for compliance.
metrics.remediation: Set tls_version = 'TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3' in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether InnoDB at-rest tablespace encryption is on via a key-management plugin. Required to protect data files from offline disclosure.
metrics.remediation: Enable TDE: configure file_key_management plugin and set innodb_encrypt_tables = ON

metrics.description: Whether binary log files are encrypted on disk (encrypt_binlog). Binlogs leak row-level data unless encrypted.
metrics.remediation: Set encrypt_binlog = ON (requires file_key_management plugin configured)

metrics.description: Days remaining before the SSL/TLS certificate expires. Expired certs break TLS connections and trigger client failures.
metrics.remediation: Renew SSL certificate before expiration

metrics.description: Whether the built-in server_audit plugin is loaded and recording events. Required for security investigation and compliance trails.
metrics.remediation: Install built-in audit plugin: INSTALL PLUGIN server_audit SONAME 'server_audit.so'; set server_audit_logging = ON

metrics.description: Whether the slow query log is on. Required for performance triage and security forensic review of long-running statements.
metrics.remediation: Set slow_query_log = ON and long_query_time in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether the error log writes to a persistent file (log_error). Required to retain crash and warning context after a restart.
metrics.remediation: Set log_error to a persistent file path in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether log-raw is off. log-raw causes the server to record passwords in cleartext in the general/slow logs.
metrics.remediation: Ensure --log-raw is NOT set in my.cnf (logs passwords in cleartext)

metrics.description: Log retention duration. Must cover the compliance and incident-investigation window (typically 90+ days).
metrics.remediation: Configure log rotation to retain logs for compliance period

metrics.description: Whether the root account is restricted to local hosts only. Remote root access dramatically widens the breach surface.
metrics.remediation: DELETE FROM mysql.user WHERE User='root' AND Host NOT IN ('localhost','127.0.0.1','::1')

metrics.description: Number of accounts holding the SUPER privilege. SUPER bypasses most safety controls and should be limited to break-glass roles.
metrics.remediation: Revoke SUPER from unnecessary accounts; use granular privileges instead

metrics.description: Count of anonymous (empty username) accounts. Anonymous accounts allow unauthenticated access and must not exist on production.
metrics.remediation: DROP USER ''@'localhost'; DROP USER ''@'%';

metrics.description: Count of accounts allowed from wildcard '%' hosts that hold excessive privileges. Such accounts dramatically widen exposure.
metrics.remediation: Restrict user accounts to specific hosts rather than '%' wildcard

metrics.description: Number of accounts holding GRANT OPTION. Excess holders can self-escalate privileges and propagate access uncontrollably.
metrics.remediation: Revoke GRANT OPTION from accounts that do not need to delegate privileges

metrics.description: Disk-usage percentage on the MariaDB data directory volume. Above 85% raises the risk of write failures and crash on full.
metrics.remediation: Add disk capacity or archive/purge old data

metrics.description: Projected days until InnoDB data files exhaust their volume. Short windows demand capacity action or data lifecycle work.
metrics.remediation: Plan capacity expansion or implement data lifecycle management

metrics.description: Table-level data-free percentage (fragmentation). High fragmentation wastes disk and degrades scan performance.
metrics.remediation: Run OPTIMIZE TABLE or ALTER TABLE ... ENGINE=InnoDB to reclaim space

metrics.description: Whether the Aria engine (used by internal MariaDB tables) has adequate disk space and log capacity.
metrics.remediation: Monitor aria_pagecache_buffer_size; ensure Aria log files have adequate space

metrics.description: Whether total data directory size is being measured over time. Required for trend-based capacity forecasting.
metrics.remediation: Configure monitoring for MariaDB data directory size growth

metrics.description: Active connection count as a percentage of max_connections. High utilization risks ER_CON_COUNT_ERROR rejections under load.
metrics.remediation: Increase max_connections or enable built-in thread pool (thread_handling = pool-of-threads)

metrics.description: Whether the built-in thread pool (thread_handling=pool-of-threads) is on. Recommended for high-concurrency workloads to bound resource use.
metrics.remediation: Set thread_handling = pool-of-threads in my.cnf for better high-concurrency performance (built-in, no Enterprise license needed)

metrics.description: Aborted connections as a percentage of total. High rates point to network issues, packet limits, or short timeouts.
metrics.remediation: Investigate aborted connections: check max_allowed_packet, wait_timeout, net_read_timeout

metrics.description: Peak Max_used_connections versus max_connections. Less than 20% headroom risks rejections during traffic spikes.
metrics.remediation: Review Max_used_connections vs max_connections; resize or enable thread pool

metrics.description: Thread cache hit rate (when not using pool-of-threads). Low hit rates indicate frequent thread creation overhead — a performance / caching concern. Moved from capacity_connections in v1.3.0 per docs/guides/metric-placement-review.md §2A.
metrics.remediation: Increase thread_cache_size if not using pool-of-threads mode

metrics.display_name: InnoDB Buffer Pool Hit Ratio Healthy
metrics.description: InnoDB buffer pool hit ratio. Low values indicate the working set exceeds RAM, causing disk-bound reads; healthy values depend on workload type — OLTP workloads should sit near 99%, OLAP workloads with working sets larger than RAM operate healthily lower. Moved from capacity_maintenance in v1.3.0 per docs/guides/metric-placement-review.md §2A.
metrics.remediation: Increase innodb_buffer_pool_size (target 70-80% of available RAM)

metrics.description: InnoDB purge lag (history list length, in rows). Sustained growth points to long-running transactions blocking undo cleanup; write-heavy OLTP workloads naturally accumulate more undo than read-heavy or analytical workloads.
metrics.remediation: Investigate long-running transactions causing purge lag; check innodb_max_purge_lag

metrics.description: Number of large tables exceeding 30% fragmentation. Such tables benefit from OPTIMIZE TABLE during a maintenance window.
metrics.remediation: Run OPTIMIZE TABLE for heavily fragmented tables during maintenance window

metrics.description: Whether table statistics are kept fresh via innodb_stats_auto_recalc. Stale stats lead to bad query plans.
metrics.remediation: Run ANALYZE TABLE on tables with stale statistics; enable innodb_stats_auto_recalc

metrics.description: Whether the event scheduler is on (when MariaDB events are used). If off, scheduled maintenance events do not fire.
metrics.remediation: Set event_scheduler = ON if using MariaDB events for maintenance tasks

metrics.description: Whether aria_pagecache_buffer_size is sized for the Aria/internal-table workload. Undersizing degrades internal-table I/O.
metrics.remediation: Set aria_pagecache_buffer_size to at least 128M if Aria engine is in active use

metrics.description: Highest AUTO_INCREMENT consumption across columns. Approaching the data-type max risks insert failures (ER_AUTOINC_READ_FAILED).
metrics.remediation: Alter column to BIGINT UNSIGNED or use sequences before reaching INT/BIGINT limit

metrics.description: Projected days until the data volume is full. Less than 6 months requires a capacity plan or archival strategy.
metrics.remediation: Plan storage expansion or data archival strategy

metrics.description: Whether a recurring capacity review (typically quarterly) takes place. Without it, growth surprises can outrun procurement.
metrics.remediation: Establish a regular capacity review process

metrics.description: Whether large tables use partitioning. Partitioning helps manageability (rolling purge) and pruning-based performance.
metrics.remediation: Consider partitioning tables exceeding 100M rows; MariaDB supports range, list, hash, key partitioning

metrics.display_name: Buffer Pool Read Hit Rate Healthy
metrics.description: InnoDB buffer pool read hit rate. Low values indicate the working set spills to disk and degrades latency; healthy values depend on workload type — OLTP workloads should sit near 99%, OLAP workloads with working sets larger than RAM operate healthily lower.
metrics.remediation: Increase innodb_buffer_pool_size; target 70-80% of total RAM

metrics.description: Whether the query cache is off or DEMAND-only. The cache was deprecated in 10.1.7 and removed in 10.11; leaving it ON adds contention.
metrics.remediation: Set query_cache_type = 0 in my.cnf; query cache removed in MariaDB 10.11

metrics.description: Aria page cache hit rate for internal table operations. Sustained low rates degrade internal-query latency.
metrics.remediation: Increase aria_pagecache_buffer_size if Aria cache hit rate is low

metrics.description: Hit ratio of table_open_cache. Low ratios cause repeated table-open syscalls and waste CPU.
metrics.remediation: Increase table_open_cache if Opened_tables/Uptime ratio is high

metrics.description: Whether join_buffer_size is sized for the join-heavy workload. Per-session allocation makes oversizing risky.
metrics.remediation: Tune join_buffer_size based on workload; default 256K is usually sufficient

metrics.description: Whether performance_schema is on. Required to surface per-query and per-wait diagnostics for tuning.
metrics.remediation: Set performance_schema = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether the slow query log is on. Required for systematic discovery of long-running and expensive statements.
metrics.remediation: Set slow_query_log = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Slow-query threshold (long_query_time). Values above 1s under-capture problematic queries from the slow log.
metrics.remediation: Set long_query_time = 1 (or lower) in my.cnf to capture slow queries

metrics.description: Whether log_queries_not_using_indexes is on. Required to flag full-scan queries for indexing review.
metrics.remediation: Set log_queries_not_using_indexes = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether top queries (Performance Schema or slow log) get periodic review. Without review, regressions go unaddressed.
metrics.remediation: Review performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest or use pt-query-digest

metrics.description: Share of queries doing full table scans. Sustained high rates indicate missing indexes or bad plans; analytical (OLAP) workloads naturally generate more scans than OLTP, where indexes should cover most access patterns.
metrics.remediation: Add indexes to eliminate full table scans; use EXPLAIN to identify queries

metrics.description: Whether MariaDB user statistics (userstat) are on. Required for per-user and per-table I/O attribution.
metrics.remediation: Set userstat = ON in my.cnf for enhanced per-user and per-table statistics (MariaDB-specific feature)

metrics.description: Number of InnoDB row-lock waits. High counts point to contention or long-running write transactions; write-heavy OLTP workloads tolerate more row-lock waits than read-heavy or analytical workloads.
metrics.remediation: Investigate blocking queries via information_schema.INNODB_LOCK_WAITS; optimize transactions

metrics.description: Recent InnoDB deadlock count. Sustained deadlocks indicate inconsistent locking order at the application layer.
metrics.remediation: Enable innodb_print_all_deadlocks = ON; review application transaction order

metrics.description: Volume of metadata-lock waits. High counts indicate DDL is being blocked by long-running transactions; high-concurrency OLTP environments should tolerate near-zero waits because a single waiting DDL stalls all dependent sessions.
metrics.remediation: Check information_schema.METADATA_LOCK_INFO; ensure DDLs run when no long transactions are open

metrics.description: Share of time the Galera cluster spends in flow control. Sustained pauses indicate a slow node throttling the cluster.
metrics.remediation: Reduce write load on slow Galera nodes; tune wsrep_provider_options flow control parameters

metrics.description: Replica lag in seconds (Seconds_Behind_Master). Lag above 30s breaks read-after-write expectations and DR readiness.
metrics.remediation: Investigate replica SQL thread lag; consider parallel replication (slave_parallel_threads)

metrics.description: Whether the replica SQL thread is applying events. If stopped, the replica falls behind and DR readiness degrades.
metrics.remediation: Check SHOW REPLICA STATUS; investigate and restart replica SQL thread

metrics.description: Whether the replica IO thread is connected to its source. If disconnected, no new binlog events arrive on the replica.
metrics.remediation: Check network connectivity to source; review replica error log

metrics.description: Whether wsrep_cluster_size matches the expected node count. A mismatch points to a partitioned or split cluster.
metrics.remediation: Investigate split-brain risk; ensure all Galera nodes are joined (wsrep_local_state_comment = Synced)

metrics.description: Whether the running MariaDB major version is current and supported (10.11+ LTS). Older majors lose security patches.
metrics.remediation: Upgrade to MariaDB 10.11 LTS (current LTS) or MariaDB 11.4 LTS

metrics.description: Whether the latest minor/patch release within the major version is applied. Falling behind misses bug and security fixes.
metrics.remediation: Apply latest MariaDB patch release for bug fixes and security patches

metrics.description: Whether the MariaDB version is within active support (not EOL). EOL versions stop receiving security patches.
metrics.remediation: Upgrade from EOL MariaDB version; consult MariaDB lifecycle page

metrics.description: Whether all user tables use InnoDB. MyISAM lacks crash recovery and row-level locking and is unsuitable for transactional data.
metrics.remediation: Convert MyISAM tables to InnoDB: ALTER TABLE t ENGINE = InnoDB

metrics.description: Whether the deployment tracks an LTS release (10.11 or 11.4). LTS tracks reduce upgrade churn and broaden vendor support.
metrics.remediation: Prefer MariaDB 10.11 LTS or 11.4 LTS over short-term maintenance releases for production

metrics.description: Whether a high-availability solution (Galera Cluster, MaxScale/HAProxy with replication) is in place. Required to bound downtime during node failure.
metrics.remediation: Implement Galera Cluster or MariaDB MaxScale for automatic failover (MariaDB does NOT use InnoDB Cluster or Group Replication)

metrics.description: Whether a database proxy (MaxScale or ProxySQL) fronts MariaDB. Provides transparent failover, query routing, and load balancing.
metrics.remediation: Deploy MariaDB MaxScale for connection pooling, query routing, and failover transparency

metrics.description: Whether innodb_strict_mode is on. Required to prevent silent truncation and surface DDL/DML errors during inserts.
metrics.remediation: Set innodb_strict_mode = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether a documented MariaDB upgrade plan exists. Required to upgrade ahead of EOL without emergency cutovers.
metrics.remediation: Document upgrade path and schedule before current version approaches EOL

metrics.description: Whether sql_mode includes STRICT_TRANS_TABLES and NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION. Required to surface invalid data and engine fallbacks.
metrics.remediation: Add STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION to sql_mode in my.cnf

metrics.description: Count of deprecated MariaDB features used by stored routines. Deprecated features can break on a future major upgrade.
metrics.remediation: Review MariaDB changelog for deprecated features; test upgrade in staging first

metrics.description: Count of user-data tables still using MyISAM. MyISAM lacks crash recovery and row-level locking; counts above zero are legacy debt.
metrics.remediation: Convert MyISAM tables to InnoDB for crash recovery and row-level locking

metrics.description: Whether databases and tables use the utf8mb4 character set. Required for full Unicode coverage including emoji and supplementary planes.
metrics.remediation: Set character_set_server = utf8mb4 and collation_server = utf8mb4_unicode_ci in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether MariaDB system-versioned (temporal) tables are used where appropriate. Provides built-in audit history without trigger plumbing.
metrics.remediation: Consider using MariaDB system-versioned tables (WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING) for audit history (unique MariaDB feature not in MySQL)

metrics.description: Whether the MariaDB instance is wired into a monitoring system (PMM, Zabbix, etc.). Required to detect anomalies and saturation early.
metrics.remediation: Connect MariaDB to Percona Monitoring and Management (PMM) or Zabbix

metrics.description: Whether alerts cover critical MariaDB metrics (lag, flow control, connections, disk). Required to drive paging on incidents.
metrics.remediation: Configure alerts for replication lag, Galera flow control, connection saturation, disk usage

metrics.description: Whether slow-query logs are analyzed on a recurring basis (e.g., pt-query-digest). Without analysis, regressions accumulate unseen.
metrics.remediation: Use pt-query-digest or analyze performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest periodically

metrics.description: Whether schema and configuration changes pass through a controlled change-management process. Required to avoid undocumented drift.
metrics.remediation: Implement schema migration tooling (Liquibase, Flyway) and change approval process

metrics.description: Whether GTIDs are consistent between source and replica (no errant transactions). Errant transactions break safe failover.
metrics.remediation: Investigate errant transactions using GTID_SUBTRACT(); use pt-table-checksum

metrics.description: Whether the server build supports SSL/TLS (have_ssl=YES). Required as a precondition for encrypting client connections.
metrics.remediation: Ensure MySQL is compiled with SSL support and ssl-ca/ssl-cert/ssl-key are configured

metrics.description: Whether an audit plugin (MySQL Enterprise Audit or community audit) is loaded and recording events. Required for compliance trails.
metrics.remediation: Install audit plugin: INSTALL PLUGIN audit_log SONAME 'audit_log.so'

metrics.description: Whether innodb_buffer_pool_size is sized for the workload (typically 70-80% of RAM on dedicated hosts). Undersizing forces disk-bound reads.
metrics.remediation: Set innodb_buffer_pool_size to 70-80% of available RAM for dedicated database servers

metrics.description: Whether total database data size (DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH) is being captured. Required for trend-based growth and capacity planning.
metrics.remediation: Monitor total data size growth trends for capacity planning

metrics.description: Whether innodb_buffer_pool_instances is sized for the pool. Misconfiguration causes contention or wasted memory on multi-GB pools.
metrics.remediation: Set innodb_buffer_pool_instances = 1 per GB of buffer pool (max 8-16)

metrics.description: Whether innodb_log_file_size (or innodb_redo_log_capacity) is sized for the write workload. Undersizing causes frequent flush stalls.
metrics.remediation: Tune innodb_log_file_size (or innodb_redo_log_capacity in MySQL 8.0.30+)

metrics.description: Whether SELECT throughput (Com_select) is being captured. Required to track query-rate trends and detect regressions.
metrics.remediation: Enable Performance Schema and monitor Com_select counter for throughput trends

metrics.description: Whether key_buffer_size is kept minimal on InnoDB-only deployments. Oversizing wastes RAM that should go to the InnoDB buffer pool.
metrics.remediation: Reduce key_buffer_size to ~8M if not using MyISAM tables

metrics.description: Whether sort_buffer_size is in the safe range (256K-4M). It is allocated per session, so oversizing exhausts memory under load.
metrics.remediation: Tune sort_buffer_size based on workload; avoid setting too large (per-session allocation)

metrics.description: Rate of filesort merge passes. High counts indicate sorts spilling to disk; usually mitigated by indexes or larger sort buffers.
metrics.remediation: Add indexes to ORDER BY / GROUP BY columns; increase sort_buffer_size

metrics.description: Share of table-level lock waits. High ratios indicate residual MyISAM tables; InnoDB uses row-level locking.
metrics.remediation: Migrate MyISAM tables to InnoDB; InnoDB uses row-level locking

metrics.description: Count of accounts still using the deprecated mysql_native_password plugin. Migration is required ahead of plugin removal.
metrics.remediation: Migrate accounts to caching_sha2_password: ALTER USER x IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password
